blocks.text: Thermochemistry is the study of the quantity of heat energy absorbed or evolved during physical or chemical changes; it is also called energetics and is largely based on the first law of thermodynamics. Hess's law, a special case of the first law, is a remarkable tool in a chemist's hand with numerous applications in analytical chemistry, and thermodynamics also predicts whether a particular reaction can occur under specified conditions, that is, the spontaneity of a reaction.

blocks.title: Enthalpy and enthalpy change
blocks.text: The energy possessed by a substance due to its structure (types of bonds) and physical state is its heat content or enthalpy, H. Every substance has a characteristic enthalpy, so the total enthalpy of the products (HP) is never equal to that of the reactants (HR), and a reaction brings a change in enthalpy, delta H = HP - HR: the net energy evolved or absorbed as heat.

items: HP is less than HR: the enthalpy falls, heat equal to HP - HR is evolved, and delta H is negative. A chemical reaction or physical change in which heat is evolved from the system to the surroundings is an exothermic process; the combustion of carbon in oxygen, C(s) + O2(g) gives CO2(g), has delta H = -393.7 kJ per mol.

HP is greater than HR: the enthalpy rises, heat equal to HP - HR is absorbed, and delta H is positive. A reaction or change in which heat is absorbed by the system from the surroundings is an endothermic process; the dissolution of ammonium chloride in water, NH4Cl(s) giving NH4+(aq) + Cl-(aq), has delta H = +16.2 kJ per mol.

blocks.alt: Two enthalpy diagrams. (a) Enthalpy axis with HR above HP; a blue 'reactants' level at HR, a red arrow down to a blue 'products' level at HP, with the note: because HR > HP, therefore delta H = negative. (b) HR below HP; a blue 'reactants' level at HR, a red arrow up to a blue 'products' level at HP, with the note: because HR < HP, therefore delta H = positive. The x-axis of each is 'Progress of Reaction'.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.1: Enthalpy diagram of (a) exothermic reaction and (b) endothermic reaction (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.1).

blocks.title: Interesting information
blocks.text: The endothermic dissolution of ammonium chloride is used in cold packs (ice packs) for injuries: kneading the pack mixes water and NH4Cl crystals, energy is absorbed from the surroundings, and the pack feels cold.
